newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish industry targets overseas firms - survey.
newsitem.headline: Irish industry targets overseas firms - survey.

text.p: Almost half of Irish companies expect to buy overseas firms or organisations over the next five years, a survey conducted by accountancy consultants Deloitte & Touche and state body Forbairt revealed on Monday.
The survey, which focused on chief executives of Irish-based companies, formed the basis of a seminar held in Dublin under the theme "Should Irish Companies remain in Irish Hands".

A statement on the survey said 29 percent of the 248 companies surveyed had purchased overseas companies in the past 10 years and the majority of those intending to invest overseas in the next five years said they will invest in UK companies.
The survey indicated that there was a general confidence in the future performance of the Irish economy.

"Above all the survey illustrates that Irish chief executives are confident that the Irish economy will continue to grow and that this confidence in the economy is translating into growth in sales and employment," Deloitte & Touche managing partner Paul McCarthy said.

The survey also indicated that Ireland was witnessing the emergence of a number of small, multinational companies that intend to expand overseas and raise capital on international markets. It also showed that nearly 30 percent of chief executives expected their companies to be sold or to seek outside investment in the near future.
Almost three-quarters of those surveyed expected employment to grow in 1997 and 65 percent reported an increase in their own workforce during the past year.
Just under 50 percent believed the creation of a Single European Market had benefited their businesses while approximately the same amount said it had no affect on their business.
